content: nu .fabro/scripts/push-gate.nu && but push main — never pipe the gate (a piped exit code is the pipe member's; fabro 2026-10-02 incident). Fresh-repo bootstrap needed a one-time git root-commit push because gitbutler requires an origin HEAD before but setup can set its target; all content commits go through but.
NEVER run seeds sync or ml sync in this repo under GitButler; commit .seeds/ and .mulch/ changes explicitly via but commit in the same batch as the code change (fabro iterate precedent).

nu .fabro/scripts/push-gate.nu && but push <branch> — never pipe the gate (a piped exit code is the pipe member's; fabro 2026-10-02 incident). PR leg until forge auth: gh pr create + gh pr merge --auto --squash (fabro precedent). Local landing NEVER pushes main directly; the workspace follows origin/main with but pull.

nu .fabro/scripts/push-gate.nu && but push <branch> — never pipe the gate (a piped exit code is the pipe member's; fabro 2026-10-02 incident). Landing: but push + but pr new + but pr auto-merge into main (forge auth valid since 2026-10-03; gh was the interim leg). The workspace follows origin/main with but pull.

description: but pr auto-merge engages auto-merge with merge-method MERGE; main requires linear history — the merge never lands.
resolution: After but pr auto-merge <sel>, ALWAYS re-arm with gh pr merge <n> --auto --squash (PR #3 lesson 2026-10-03: auto-merge enabled at MERGE and stalled silently until re-armed with squash). Recorded in AGENTS.md landing-work bullet.

title: Local iterate sprint system (nu-agent port, but-based, fabro-independent)
rationale: VCS HALF SUPERSEDED 2026-10-17 (mulch-6817): 'use but instead of git' is retired with the GitButler experiment — the loop commits with plain git (batched .seeds/.mulch, lane push through the push gate, PR-only landing to main). The 'fabro-independent' framing was separately corrected 2026-10-06: mulch is STANDALONE and its lib is fabro's native engine (see the lane-push amendment decision). ORIGINAL directive 2026-10-03: work locally for now; same sprint system as nu-agent; the sprint system is independent of the fabro develop line; use but instead of git; delegate worthwhile tasks to subagents.

description: The ml-ref-prober report cited byte sizes (1395/4230) that did not match the actual artifacts (1421/4322) — always pin parity templates from the BYTES (snapshots/files), never from a report transcript; the differential battery against the live reference is the real gate. Resolution: fixtures copied byte-identically from the probe workdir, verified against both snapshots.
resolution: Trust bytes over prose; verify via live differential runs.

title: Architecture gate @ sprint 3: five deepening candidates
rationale: Deepening pays off where the remaining ~20 parity commands each touch the same store; the gate ran after the third sprint as the loop requires.

description: Sprint 4 (mulch-8204): while moving the strict reader behind a lib seam, the first cut dropped the CLI flag that the old call sites passed (`--allow-unknown-types`), so three commands accepted the flag and silently ignored it — a regression the 65-test battery could not see (no test exercised the flag on those commands).
resolution: read_records(domain, allow_unknown) takes the flag explicitly; before/after call-site diff of every flag that reaches a moved function. LESSON: when a function moves behind a seam, diff the ARGUMENTS of every call site, not just the behaviour of the new path.

description: Anchor-based test edits break after `cargo fmt` runs on an uncommitted insert: the formatter rewraps macro args, so exact anchors from the written buffer stop matching the file. Re-read the formatted file region BEFORE constructing the old/new anchor pair (cost: one failed assert in sprint 5).
resolution: Re-read the formatted region before composing anchor pairs; never anchor on unformatted memory of a write.

description: Sprint 6 front-ran part of mulch-ca49 to make the batch envelope differential-testable: added updated/errors/warnings to the batch json envelopes (ccf6's 'reports updated in its counters'). Deliberate, noted in the commit; ca49 keeps the PLAIN surface (Skip:/Create:/Update: lines, Would process count, Skipped N duplicates line, Created 0 line) and the create-only compact rewrite. Rule of thumb: when a parity ticket needs json fields another seed owns, taking the fields is fine IF the commit message says so and the seed stays open for the rest.
resolution: Fields taken deliberately, seed kept open for the plain surface.

title: Sprint-6 architecture gate
rationale: State 6/6 with 6 % 3 == 0 and last review at sprint 3 — the every-3rd-sprint gate is due right after the ccf6 closeout.

description: `seeds update --description` REPLACES the whole description — appending an update requires fetch-current-then-write-full. Hit TWICE in one session (arch-gate reassessments, 00aa probe notes): both times the original text was silently lost and had to be rebuilt from session context. Mitigation: always use a seeds_append helper (show --format json -> current description + addition -> update), never a bare update for addenda.
resolution: Append-only helper bound in the session; consider filing a seeds CLI --description-append feature.

description: Deleting a function by slicing from its doc-comment start to the next `pub fn` can swallow the NEXT function's doc block when anchors drift (sprint 8: read_lines deletion ate read_records' docs; standards review caught it). Deletion guard: after any slice-based delete, grep-verify the SURVIVOR's doc block still sits flush above it — same class as the insert-anchor guard, mirrored for deletions.
resolution: Deletion guard added to the session checklist; iterate skill edit-verification guard already covers region re-reads.

name: expect-over-dead-fallback
description: When a fallback is provably unreachable (e.g. `id().unwrap_or(input)` where the resolver only matches identified records), the code should `expect("invariant")` rather than keep a silent default: the default hides the invariant and can contradict the stated contract (sprint 9 standards review). Mirrored reference JS (`record.id ?? id`) is not a reason to keep dead defaults — name the dead fallback in a comment instead.

name: compare-stderr-too
description: A differential test that compares only STDOUT can pass while the stderr rendering regresses (sprint 10: plain `validate` prints its details on stderr — the const-sub-error spacing bug survived a green battery). Rule: for every command whose details/errors render on stderr, compare stderr too, or say in the test why not (network-bound lines like doctor's update check).

title: retro 2026-10-06: gate recipe, reference-source pointer, match-order rule, seeds json shape
rationale: Retro 2026-10-06 (sprint 15 + arch gate), four loop-asset changes: (1) iterate skill quality gates now default to `timeout 600 just qualitygate` per commit round — the nushell recipe cannot mask a result the way a bash pipe can (two masked gate failures this sprint: cargo build|tail EXIT=0 on a failed build, fmt --check|head FMT_RC=0 on diffs); sprint end keeps one full-workspace nextest battery; raw cargo commands stay owned by AGENTS.md. (2) AGENTS.md carries a one-line pointer to the reference ml TS source (mise where npm:@os-eco/mulch-cli -> node_modules/@os-eco/mulch-cli/src; fallback readlink -f $(command -v ml)) — this session burned ~6 calls rediscovering it. (3) rust-style-guide control-flow: match-arm ORDER is semantics when earlier arms are more specific; merging same-body arms (clippy match_same_arms) must preserve order, pinned by comment+test — clippy's own fix text can reorder arms silently (caught only by a unit test). NOTE: this rule exists ONLY in the repo-local .agents/ copy; the .fabro/skills original lacks it — carry it over on the next drift-refresh or let the fabro line adopt it via its own seed. (4) docs/agents/issue-tracker.md documents the seeds json shapes (single id -> issue, multi -> issues).

title: iterate lane pushes at closeout (amendment 2026-10-06)
rationale: PUSH MECHANIC AMENDED 2026-10-17 (mulch-6817): after the GitButler teardown the closeout push is 'nu .fabro/scripts/push-gate.nu' (exit 0) then 'git push origin iterate' in the same unpiped cell; everything else in this decision stands. CORRECTED FRAMING (user correction 2026-10-06 evening, same day as the amendment): mulch is a STANDALONE tool — the mulch CLI is its own product — while crates/mulch (the lib) is simultaneously the native expertise engine denkhaus/fabro embeds. The iterate loop is mulch's OWN development loop, not a satellite of the fabro develop line; 'independence from fabro' was the wrong frame. What stays: lane pushes to origin/iterate at every sprint closeout (push gate, exit 0, then the push) for cross-machine availability — pushing the branch is not landing; PRs/main integration stay explicit-user-order-only (engine flow). NEW consequence of the corrected framing: the lib's public API is an integration surface for fabro — lib API changes are integration-relevant and deserve that lens in review (the standalone-tool-plus-embedded-crate posture now also sits in README's Product posture paragraph).

title: Two surgical iterate-loop changes after sprints 19-21: commit-integrity check (but status under-reports; verify the committed file list) and reviewer-handoff git hashes
rationale: BOTH SURVIVE in plain-git form after the GitButler teardown (2026-10-17, mulch-6817): the integrity check now lists intended files with git status --short + git diff --name-only, stages explicit paths and verifies the landed list with git show --stat <hash>; reviewers are always handed resolvable git hashes (git log --grep=<seed> --format=%h -1) — the unresolvable-but-commit-id half of the problem retired with the tool. ORIGINAL (sprints 19-21): both frictions cost real work in consecutive sprints: sprint 20 shipped a commit whose message claimed 7/7 collapsed sites while the worktree change to records.rs never entered the commit (but status hid the file), and sprint-20/21 reviewers each lost time resolving a but-commit id that git cannot show. The rest of the loop held (both review gates caught real issues, probe-first paid off in sprint 19).

title: Multi-seed sprints run as parallel subagents on GitButler lanes above iterate
rationale: MECHANISM SUPERSEDED 2026-10-17 (mulch-6817): the GitButler lanes are retired — the protocol now runs all chain links as SIMULTANEOUS subagents in ONE worktree with DISJOINT file ownership, and the HOST commits each delivery (git add <that child's paths> && git commit, one commit per child; children never touch git). Unchanged: the user directive to run chain links as simultaneous subagents, host-folded shared files, host-side fmt/clippy/battery gates, read-only reviewers. ORIGINAL (user directive 2026-10-11): work with subagents and use GitButler for simultaneous work in the same codebase. Sprint 22 proved the protocol for one crate + big battery: three chain links, three lanes, zero cross-lane incidents.

title: Host pre-lands shared seams before spawning parallel lanes
rationale: Sprint 23: the failure_envelope constructor was the only edge between lane A and lane B; pre-landing it removed the dependency for the cost of one small host commit.

title: The shipped binary carries no ml references: it promotes mulch everywhere (prime and Retry echo included); ml stays the working tool + reference until feature parity
rationale: mulch replaces ml at the self-hosting cutover (mulch-96ed); any user-facing text promoting the retired binary works against that. ml stays in use as tool+reference only during the parity phase, which is process, not binary output.

content: Long 'but commit -m' strings get mangled by the shell (backticks inside double quotes run command substitution — sprint 25 lost the pup message's quoted parts and needed a reword). Rule: long commit messages go through a file — write /tmp/msg.txt, commit with -m "$(cat /tmp/msg.txt)", verify the landed message with but show <id> (the commit-integrity check already demands listing intended files before and git show --stat after).

title: ORIENT checks lane staleness before trusting the worktree
rationale: STILL IN FORCE; mechanism changed with the GitButler teardown 2026-10-17 (mulch-6817): git fetch, then compare .iterate-state.json against the lane's top commit message, then git rebase origin/iterate (never with a dirty worktree or a background cargo running). The but-era catch-up dance (unapply sibling lanes / but branch update / re-apply) is gone with the tool. ORIGINAL (sprint 29): but status no-changes does not imply a current worktree — another machine may have moved origin/iterate; the catch-up dance (unapply sibling lanes, update, re-apply non-colliding) failed twice before succeeding in sprint 29

description: GitButler cross-machine lane catch-up (mulch, 2026-10-15): origin/iterate had moved 4 sprints on another machine while this workspace stayed applied at the old tip — but status parsed fine and showed "no changes", so the stale worktree only surfaced via .iterate-state.json disagreeing with the lane commits. Direct `but branch update iterate` FAILED: "Failed to merge bases while cherry picking <workspace commit> ... conflict ... 17fb074, cb4f325" — the workspace merge commit could not be rebuilt because a SECOND applied lane (chore/but-fork-6) touches .mise.toml lines adjacent to origin/iterate additions (fused hunk collision; the but fork.6/fork.7 patches addressed this class but the workspace-commit cherry-pick still dies). Working dance: `but unapply <other-lane>` then `but branch update iterate` (succeeds instantly), leaving the other lane UNAPPLIED — its re-apply collides with the new base (adjacent .mise.toml lines), so the pin content must land on the moved base or the lane waits for a rebased duplicate. ORIENT rule: compare the state file against the lane commits BEFORE trusting the worktree; never assume but status healthy = worktree current.
resolution: unapply the colliding sibling lane (chore/but-fork-6), but branch update iterate, keep the sibling unapplied until its mise pin lands on the moved base; ORIENT now checks state-file-vs-lane-commit staleness first (skill change sprint 29)

title: Sprint notes rotate out of the state file
rationale: The notes array grows one long entry per sprint and every session start reads the whole state file; brightctl hit the 50-KB read-tool limit at 222 notes. Rotation keeps the working set small while the JSONL archive stays git-diffable history.

name: gitbutler-remote-rewrite-conflict-discard
description: RETIRED 2026-10-17 (GitButler teardown, mulch-6817) — kept as history: the tool, 'but branch update' and the oplog 'but discard' no longer exist. ORIGINAL RECIPE: When another machine history-edits the pushed lane (split/rebase of a commit that exists locally, e.g. a squashed sprint commit re-split remotely), but branch update <lane> integrates the remote stack and leaves the stale LOCAL duplicate {conflicted} atop it. Resolution: verify the local commit's content is contained in the remote stack (diff local-commit vs the remote code-equivalent commit; patch-id --stable on crates/ if bases differ), then 'but discard <commit-id>' (oplog-undoable) — never resolve hunk-by-hunk, the workspace already carries the newer work. The partial conflict overlay can leave a non-compiling mix in the worktree until the discard rebuilds it. WHAT SURVIVES: before integrating a moved remote branch, prove containment first (diff / patch-id --stable) and take the REMOTE side — under plain git that is commit-or-stash, then git fetch + git rebase origin/<branch>.

title: Hunk IDs come from but status -fv
rationale: RETIRED 2026-10-17 (mulch-6817): but is gone — the hunk-id collection problem does not exist under plain git, which stages by PATH, not by hunk id. The lesson that survives is the commit-integrity check: list intended files first (git status --short + git diff --name-only), stage explicit paths, verify the landed list with git show --stat <hash>. ORIGINAL (2026-10-17): three times in one session a multi-hunk file's ID set was under-collected by grepping but diff's box headers — the wrapped box layout hides headers; the integrity check had to catch each miss via amend. but status -fv lists hunk IDs per file reliably.

content: Plain-git VCS conventions (GitButler retired 2026-10-17, mulch-6817 — supersedes the five but-era variants mx-bc4df7/mx-a883c3/mx-9af32f/mx-dc1a6d/mx-4d91cf): (1) PUSH = 'nu .fabro/scripts/push-gate.nu' (exit 0) then 'git push origin <branch>' in the SAME unpiped cell — never pipe the gate (a piped exit code is the pipe member's; fabro 2026-10-02 incident); (2) local landing NEVER pushes main directly: 'gh pr merge <n> --auto --squash' (main requires linear history), the local lane follows origin/main with git fetch + git rebase; (3) commit .seeds/ and .mulch/ explicitly in the SAME commit as the change they document — seeds sync/ml sync open their own commits, so they stay out of the batch flow (seeds sync --status / --dry-run is the pending-change check); (4) long commit messages go through a file (git commit -F /tmp/msg.txt) — inline -m strings with quotes/backticks get shell-mangled (sprint 25); (5) the one-time empty root commit 235a70d was a gitbutler bootstrap exception, now historical — no content ever landed that way.
